3-1.title: What Is Energy?
3-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS

Energy is the ability to do work or cause change. Two important kinds are:
- Kinetic energy = the energy of MOTION. Anything moving has kinetic energy.
- Potential energy = STORED energy because of an object's position or condition (like a ball at the top of a hill, or a stretched rubber band).

What changes kinetic energy: MORE mass and MORE speed both give MORE kinetic energy. Of the two, speed has an especially strong effect.

Example 1 — Ball on a hill
A ball at the top of a hill has potential energy (stored, because of its high position). As it rolls down, that potential energy changes into kinetic energy (motion).

Example 2 — Compare kinetic energy
A fast-moving truck has more kinetic energy than a slow bike, both because the truck has more mass AND because more speed adds kinetic energy.

Example 3 — Stretched band
A stretched rubber band stores potential energy. When released, that stored energy becomes kinetic energy as the band snaps.

questions.question: Potential energy is best described as

questions.question: Which object has the MOST kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy increases with mass and especially speed, so the fast-racing car has the most.

questions.question: As a ball rolls down a hill, its energy changes from
questions.explanation: The stored potential energy at the top changes into kinetic energy of motion as the ball rolls down.

questions.question: Two balls roll at the same speed, but one has more mass. Which has more kinetic energy?

choices.C: They have the same kinetic energy

questions.question: A stretched rubber band stores potential energy. When released, that energy mainly becomes

questions.question: Two identical cars move, but Car A is faster than Car B. Which statement is true?

choices.A: Car B has more kinetic energy
choices.B: Car A has more kinetic energy

questions.explanation: With equal mass, the faster car (Car A) has more kinetic energy because more speed means more kinetic energy.

questions.question: A roller coaster car is highest at the top of the first hill and fastest at the bottom. This shows that

choices.A: potential energy is greatest at the top and kinetic energy is greatest at the bottom
choices.B: kinetic energy is greatest at the top

questions.explanation: At the top the car has the most stored potential energy; at the bottom that energy has become the most kinetic energy (motion).

3-2.title: Forms of Energy
3-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS

Energy comes in many forms, and all of them can do work and change from one form to another:
- Mechanical energy: the energy of moving objects (and stored motion energy).
- Thermal energy: from moving particles; gives us heat.
- Chemical energy: stored in food, fuel, and batteries.
- Electrical energy: from moving electric charges.
- Light energy: travels as light (radiant energy).
- Sound energy: travels as vibrations you can hear.

Example 1 — Match the form
A battery stores CHEMICAL energy. A moving bicycle has MECHANICAL energy. A glowing bulb gives off LIGHT energy. A ringing bell makes SOUND energy.

Example 2 — Heat source
The warmth from a campfire is THERMAL energy, which comes from fast-moving particles.

Example 3 — Food fuels you
The food you eat holds CHEMICAL energy that your body uses to move (mechanical) and stay warm (thermal).

questions.question: The energy stored in food, fuel, and batteries is called
questions.explanation: Chemical energy is stored in food, fuel, and batteries.

questions.question: The energy of moving particles that gives us heat is
questions.explanation: Thermal energy comes from moving particles and gives us heat.

questions.question: A moving bicycle is an example of
questions.explanation: Mechanical energy is the energy of moving objects, like a moving bicycle.

questions.question: A glowing light bulb gives off mostly
questions.explanation: A glowing bulb gives off light energy (along with some thermal energy as heat).

questions.question: A ringing bell produces which form of energy?
questions.explanation: A ringing bell vibrates and produces sound energy.

questions.question: The energy that flows through wires to run a TV is
questions.explanation: Electrical energy comes from moving electric charges and powers devices like a TV.

questions.question: Which statement about forms of energy is TRUE?

choices.B: All forms of energy can do work and can change into other forms
choices.C: Only chemical energy can do work
choices.D: Sound is not a form of energy

questions.explanation: All forms of energy can do work and can be transformed from one form into another.

questions.question: The warmth you feel near a campfire is which form of energy?
questions.explanation: The warmth from a fire is thermal energy, which comes from fast-moving particles.

questions.question: Which pairing of object and energy form is correct?

choices.C: Burning fuel releasing heat — thermal energy

questions.explanation: Burning fuel releases thermal energy (heat). The other pairings are incorrect matches.

questions.question: The food you eat holds chemical energy. Your body mainly uses this to

choices.B: power your movement and keep you warm

questions.explanation: Your body changes the chemical energy in food into mechanical energy (movement) and thermal energy (body heat).

3-3.title: Energy Transformations and Conservation
3-3.learn:
KEY IDEAS

An energy transformation is when energy changes from one form into another. Energy is constantly being transformed all around us.

The Law of Conservation of Energy says energy is NEVER created or destroyed — it only changes form. So the total amount of energy always stays the same.

Example 1 — Flashlight
A flashlight changes CHEMICAL energy (battery) into ELECTRICAL energy, then into LIGHT energy (and a little thermal energy).

Example 2 — Roller coaster
At the top of a hill the car has POTENTIAL energy. As it speeds downhill, that potential energy transforms into KINETIC energy.

Example 3 — Conservation
If a toy car starts with 100 units of energy, it still has 100 units total afterward — some may have become heat or sound, but no energy was destroyed; it just changed form.

questions.question: An energy transformation is when energy

choices.B: changes from one form into another

questions.explanation: An energy transformation is a change of energy from one form into another.

questions.question: The Law of Conservation of Energy states that energy

choices.A: can be created but not destroyed
choices.B: can be destroyed but not created
choices.C: is never created or destroyed, only changed in form

questions.explanation: Energy is never created or destroyed; it only changes form, so the total stays the same.

questions.question: A flashlight changes the chemical energy in its battery mainly into
questions.explanation: A flashlight transforms chemical energy into electrical energy and then into light energy.

questions.question: As a roller coaster speeds downhill, potential energy is transformed into
questions.explanation: The stored potential energy at the top becomes kinetic energy as the coaster speeds downhill.

questions.question: A toy car begins with 100 units of energy. After it runs, the total energy is

choices.A: still 100 units, just in different forms

questions.explanation: By the Law of Conservation of Energy, the total stays 100 units; some may have become heat or sound, but none was destroyed.

questions.question: A person eats a snack, then runs. Which transformation best describes this?
questions.explanation: The chemical energy in food is transformed into mechanical energy of the person's movement.

questions.question: When a guitar string is plucked, electrical-free, the mechanical energy of the moving string changes into
questions.explanation: The vibrating (mechanical) string transforms its energy into sound energy.

questions.question: A solar panel transforms light energy into
questions.explanation: A solar panel transforms light energy from the Sun into electrical energy.

questions.question: If energy is conserved, why does a bouncing ball eventually stop?

choices.B: Its energy changed into other forms like heat and sound, not destroyed
choices.D: Energy is not conserved for balls

questions.explanation: The ball's energy was not destroyed; it gradually transformed into heat and sound, so the ball slows and stops.

questions.question: Which statement BEST connects energy transformation and conservation?

choices.A: Energy can change form, and the total amount always stays the same
choices.B: Energy can change form, and the total amount grows
choices.C: Energy cannot change form at all
choices.D: Energy is destroyed each time it changes form

questions.explanation: Energy can transform between forms, but conservation means the total amount of energy always stays the same.
